svg.text: Side projectors, HD each (1920×1080, portrait): stage 48'×16' coverage — stage-previz-12
Plan: audience at the bottom, stage left on the right. Yellow = 48'×16' grate edge, grid = 4' decks, white dots = lenses (19' off centre, trim 22'-7"). Dim = light off the stage.

g.text: raster: pixel lands off the stage (burned)

svg.text: A · What v12 draws (Loom keystone 27.55°)
Each image a clean 40.1'×16' rectangle, 0% burned, overlap 32' wide = 67% of the stage.
Not physically achievable: the near edge sits 6.9' outside the lens's own frustum.
A UDX's keystone is digital and can only shrink inside the native raster.
B · Physical lens, v12 aim (tilt 39.61°, throw 1.16, keystone off)
Each: 77% of pixels on stage, 23% burned (past the far deck edge, up/downstage).
Overlap 30% of stage (18.6' wide band). Uncovered 0.8%: notches on the centre line.
Density 30–105 px/ft (far edge to near), median 48 px/ft.
C · Re-aimed for real pixels: tilt 47.5°, throw 1.14, keystone off, no shift
Each: 94% of pixels on stage, 6% burned. Far edge lands on the far deck edge (−23.9').
Overlap 40% of stage (25' wide band, ±12.6'). Uncovered 1.2% (centre-line notches).
Density 32–114 px/ft, median 50 px/ft.
Rasters (what each output carries)
Left of raster = far side of stage. Grid = 4' decks warped into the image.
B · SL, v12 aim
B · SR, v12 aim
C · SL, re-aimed
C · SR, re-aimed
Pixel budget per HD output (2,073,600 px)
Model: Loom's projectorMatrix with v12's live rig values, every pixel cast onto the grate top (6'-6" above the venue floor). The stage is treated as a flat plane:
burned light actually lands on the riser face and stairs upstage, the house downstage, and past the deck ends. No talent or scenery occlusion. 16:10 native aspect (UDX-4K40) with a 16:9 HD signal;
the raster here is the full 16:10 panel scaled to 1920×1080. Lens shift searched too: it bought ~1% at an unrealistic 0.6 image-width shift, so it is left out.
